author: NorthEast News Desk
body: About 46,000 Boston Public Schools students returned to classrooms Tuesday, with Mayor Michelle Wu and Superintendent Mary Skipper welcoming families at Holland Elementary, Boston 25 News reported.

The school year begins with the elementary school fully under district control after Boston exited state receivership. District leaders are also watching transportation closely as hundreds of buses resume daily service across the city.

Boston Public Schools is using GPS tracking through its Zoom system to monitor buses and student transportation. Skipper said the district is aiming for a 95% on-time bus success rate as routes settle into the new year.

The district also said about 15,000 students took part in summer learning programs. For families, the first days of school will provide the clearest test of whether the transportation changes and operational planning translate into reliable arrival and dismissal times.
The opening-day rollout also gives families a near-term measure of how well the district’s transportation technology and staffing plans are working.
dek: Boston Public Schools welcomed students Tuesday as the district began a new year with a fully district-run elementary school and a renewed focus on bus reliability.
headline: 46,000 Boston students return as schools start new year
